description.hypothesis: Stocks that close near the top of their daily range relative to the open (strong intraday buying pressure) continue to outperform over the next day; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Intraday body (close - open) divided by daily range (high - low), with +0.001 to avoid division by zero; long strong closes, short weak closes, used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: On TOPSP500 the baseline's Sharpe was -0.97: stocks that close strongly relative to their open tend to give back that move over the following days (short-term reversal, e.g. Lehmann 1990, Jegadeesh 1990), consistent with temporary liquidity-driven price pressure.
description.implementation: Negate the close-location signal to bet on reversal and average it over 5 days to spread positions over time and cut turnover. The divide-by-zero guard is scaled by close so numerator and denominator are both in price units.

description.hypothesis: Price pressure from intraday buying or selling reverses over roughly one to two weeks, not just the next few days; a longer averaging window keeps that reversal signal while trading less.
description.implementation: Same reversal signal as a101_rev_mean5, averaged over 10 days instead of 5, so each day's new information moves positions less.

description.hypothesis: For large, liquid stocks, price moves made on unusually high volume are more likely driven by liquidity or hedging demand than by new information, so they reverse more strongly (Llorente, Michaely, Saar and Wang 2002; Campbell, Grossman and Wang 1993).
description.implementation: Weight each day's close-location value by that day's volume relative to its 20-day average before the 5-day reversal average, so high-volume days dominate the signal.

description.hypothesis: The volume-weighted reversal is strongest in the first few days and fades after, so weights that decline with age match it better than an equal-weight window, and phasing old days out gradually avoids forced trades when a day leaves the window.
description.implementation: Replace the 5-day equal-weight mean with a 10-day linearly decaying average (weights 10..1, newest heaviest), giving an average lag of 3 days with today's weight 0.18 instead of 0.20.

description.hypothesis: Weekly price moves partly reverse, and the reversal bet is sized up for stocks with strong one-year momentum; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Take the opposite sign of the 7-day price change (counted twice, so only its sign matters) and scale it by 1 plus the cross-sectional rank of 250-day cumulative returns; used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: Larger weekly moves reverse more than small ones, so the size of the 7-day return carries information that sign() throws away; using it also stops whole positions flipping when a near-zero weekly change crosses zero.
description.implementation: Replace -sign(2 x 7-day price change) with the negative 7-day return, keeping the original 1-year momentum multiplier 1 + rank(1 + 250-day summed returns).

description.hypothesis: The ordering of weekly returns carries the reversal signal, but raw magnitudes let a few extreme, often news-driven movers dominate; ranking keeps the ordering while limiting any one stock's influence.
description.implementation: Replace the negative raw 7-day return with 0.5 minus its cross-sectional rank (centred, so losers are long and winners short). The momentum multiplier drops the inner '1 +', which cannot change a rank, to test whether it triggers the UNITS warning.

expression: rank(-ts_mean((close - open) / (high - low + 0.001 * close) * (volume / ts_mean(volume, 20)), 5)) + rank((0.5 - rank(close / ts_delay(close, 7))) * (1 + rank(ts_sum(returns, 250))))

description.hypothesis: Short-horizon intraday-pressure reversal (Alpha#101 family) and weekly close-to-close reversal with momentum tilt (Alpha#019 family) use different horizons and price information, so their errors are partly independent and an equal blend should have a higher Sharpe than either.
description.implementation: Cross-sectionally rank each family's best expression and add the ranks with equal weight, so neither signal's scale dominates.

description.hypothesis: When a stock's price and trading volume have been rising together, the move is likely driven by attention or crowded buying that later fades, so it underperforms; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Short stocks with a high 10-day correlation between daily open price and volume, long those with a negative correlation; used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: Crowded, attention-driven buying shows up as up-days on heavy volume and down-days on light volume; stocks with that pattern over the past two weeks subsequently underperform as the pressure fades.
description.implementation: Correlate daily returns with volume relative to its 20-day average over 10 days, and short high correlation. This replaces the baseline's correlation of open price levels with raw volume.

description.hypothesis: Short-term reversal is compensation for providing liquidity, and that compensation is larger in more volatile stocks where liquidity is scarcer (Nagel 2012), so the same reversal signal earns more there.
description.implementation: Multiply the parent's volume-weighted 5-day reversal signal by each stock's 20-day return volatility, tilting capital toward volatile names without changing the signal's horizon.

description.hypothesis: Common industry-level moves tend to continue (Moskowitz and Grinblatt 1999), while stock-specific, liquidity-driven moves reverse. Measuring each day's signal relative to close peers in the same subindustry isolates the part that reverses.
description.implementation: Subtract the subindustry average from the daily volume-weighted close-location value before the 5-day reversal average. The simulation's INDUSTRY neutralization setting is unchanged.

expression: trade_when(volume > ts_mean(volume, 20), -ts_mean(group_neutralize((close - open) / (high - low + 0.001 * close) * (volume / ts_mean(volume, 20)), subindustry), 5), -1)

description.hypothesis: New liquidity shocks, the source of the reversal, arrive on high-volume days; on quiet days changes in the 5-day signal are mostly noise, so trading on them adds turnover without adding return.
description.implementation: Wrap the parent in trade_when: update a stock's position only on days when its volume exceeds its 20-day average, otherwise hold the previous position (exit condition -1 never triggers).

description.hypothesis: Stocks with strong 1-year momentum excluding the last month keep outperforming, and the bet is taken when the stock has made a new 5-day low versus the prior week on rising volume, i.e. buying a temporary dip in a long-term winner; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Drop in the 5-day low versus its value 5 days earlier, times the rank of average daily return from day 240 to day 20, times the 5-day time-series rank of volume; used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: Stocks with high returns over the past year excluding the most recent month keep outperforming over the following months (intermediate-term momentum, Jegadeesh and Titman 1993); skipping the last month avoids the short-term reversal.
description.implementation: Cross-sectional rank of summed daily returns from day 240 to day 21 (240-day sum minus the latest 20-day sum), the momentum core of Alpha#052 without its 5-day-low and volume terms.

description.hypothesis: Stocks with volatile prices whose highs move together with volume are attention-driven and subsequently underperform, consistent with the low-volatility anomaly; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Negative rank of the 10-day standard deviation of daily highs, multiplied by the 10-day correlation between highs and volume; used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: The low-volatility effect is about risk measured in percentage terms (Ang et al. 2006); the standard deviation of the dollar price of highs mainly ranks stocks by price level, so measuring volatility with returns targets the intended mechanism.
description.implementation: Replace ts_std_dev(high, 10) with ts_std_dev(returns, 10) inside the rank; the high-volume correlation multiplier is unchanged.

description.hypothesis: Stocks with low recent return volatility earn higher risk-adjusted returns than volatile stocks (low-volatility anomaly, Ang et al. 2006), which studies measure over months rather than days.
description.implementation: Long low and short high 60-day return volatility via the negative cross-sectional rank, without the baseline's high-volume correlation term.

description.hypothesis: A close well below the day's volume-weighted average price signals late-day selling pressure that tends to reverse, so such stocks outperform next; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Rank of (VWAP - close) divided by rank of (VWAP + close); long stocks closing far below VWAP. Used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: A close below the day's volume-weighted average price reflects late-day selling pressure that reverses; the size of that pressure is the percentage gap, not the dollar gap, which in the baseline mixes in share price.
description.implementation: Rank the close-to-VWAP gap as a fraction of VWAP; long stocks closing furthest below VWAP, short those closing furthest above.

description.hypothesis: Late-day selling or buying pressure, seen as a close away from VWAP, reverses over several days rather than one, so accumulating the gap over a week keeps the signal while trading far less.
description.implementation: Average the percentage close-to-VWAP gap over 5 days before ranking.

description.hypothesis: Late-day pressure shared by a whole subindustry reflects sector news that tends to continue, while stock-specific pressure reflects liquidity demand that reverses (Moskowitz and Grinblatt 1999), so measuring the VWAP gap against close peers isolates the reversing part.
description.implementation: Subtract the subindustry average from each day's percentage close-to-VWAP gap before the 5-day average and rank.

description.hypothesis: Liquidity shocks that cause late-day price pressure arrive on high-volume days; on quiet days the VWAP gap is mostly noise, so trading on it adds turnover without return. Keeping the daily signal preserves its mostly next-day reversal.
description.implementation: Update a stock's position from the daily percentage close-to-VWAP rank only when its volume exceeds its 20-day average; otherwise hold the previous position (exit condition -1 never triggers).

description.hypothesis: Larger close-to-VWAP gaps reflect larger liquidity shocks and reverse more, so sizing positions by the size of the gap rather than its rank puts capital where the reversal is strongest.
description.implementation: Use the raw percentage close-to-VWAP gap as the position weight instead of its cross-sectional rank, keeping the high-volume-day update rule; the simulation's 8% truncation caps any single stock.

description.hypothesis: The largest liquidity shocks, the ones whose late-day pressure reverses most, occur on clearly abnormal volume; updating positions only on those days keeps the strongest signals and skips moderately active days whose gaps add turnover with less reversal.
description.implementation: Raise the trade_when volume threshold from above the 20-day average to above 1.5 times it; otherwise hold the previous position.

description.hypothesis: A close-to-VWAP gap formed on heavier volume reflects a larger liquidity shock that reverses more, so scaling each gap by relative volume puts more capital behind the strongest reversals (Llorente, Michaely, Saar and Wang 2002).
description.implementation: Multiply the raw percentage close-to-VWAP gap by volume relative to its 20-day average, keeping the same above-average-volume update rule.

description.hypothesis: Updating only on clearly elevated volume skips ordinary days whose gaps add turnover with little reversal, but too strict a threshold leaves positions stale; a moderate threshold balances the two.
description.implementation: Raise the trade_when threshold from 1.0x to 1.2x the 20-day average volume, keeping the relative-volume-weighted raw VWAP gap.

description.hypothesis: Each high-volume day is a liquidity-shock event whose late-day price pressure reverses over the next few days; positions should be opened on the event and wound down as the reversal completes, rather than held until the next event (stale) or rebuilt daily (costly).
description.implementation: On high-volume days record the relative-volume-weighted percentage close-to-VWAP gap, otherwise 0; the position is the 3-day average of these event values, so each event's position fades out after three days.

description.hypothesis: Stocks that open far above the previous day's high, close and low have overnight gaps driven by overnight order flow that tends to reverse during the day; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Negative product of the ranks of today's open minus yesterday's high, close and low; most negative for large overnight gap-ups. Used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: Overnight gaps are driven by overnight order flow and partly reverse during the following trading session; the size of the gap relative to the price, not in dollars, measures that pressure.
description.implementation: Short stocks with the largest percentage overnight gap up (open over previous close) and long the largest gaps down, via negative cross-sectional rank.

expression: -rank((open - ts_delay(high, 1)) / ts_delay(close, 1)) * rank(open / ts_delay(close, 1)) * rank((open - ts_delay(low, 1)) / ts_delay(close, 1))

description.hypothesis: Where today's open sits relative to the whole of yesterday's range (above the high, between, below the low) measures overnight pressure that reverses during the day; scaling the gaps by yesterday's close removes the share-price effect while keeping that information.
description.implementation: The baseline's three ranked gaps (open minus previous high, close and low), each divided by the previous close before ranking, multiplied together and negated.

description.hypothesis: Weekly reversal is much stronger in returns measured relative to close peers, because the common industry component tends to continue while the stock-specific component reflects temporary liquidity demand (Da, Liu and Schaumburg 2014; Moskowitz and Grinblatt 1999).
description.implementation: Subtract the subindustry average from the 7-day price ratio before ranking; the centred reversal rank and the 1-year momentum multiplier are unchanged.

description.hypothesis: A close above VWAP reflects late-day buying pressure that reverses, and the bet is sized up for stocks whose 30-day high is recent relative to others; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Negative close-minus-VWAP divided by a 2-day linear decay of the cross-sectional rank of days since the 30-day closing high; used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: Late-day buying pressure (close above VWAP) reverses more for stocks that have just set a 30-day high, where buying is likeliest to be temporary momentum chasing; the gap should be measured in percent and the recency weight kept bounded.
description.implementation: Percentage close-to-VWAP gap, negated, multiplied by one minus the smoothed rank of days since the 30-day closing high (1 for the most recent highs, 0 for the oldest), instead of dividing by that rank.

description.hypothesis: Late-day pressure reverses more after a recent 30-day high, and liquidity shocks arrive on high-volume days, so updating the recency-weighted VWAP gap only on those days should keep the reversal while cutting turnover.
description.implementation: Wrap the parent in trade_when: update positions only when volume exceeds its 20-day average, otherwise hold.

description.hypothesis: When the volume-weighted average price sits below the geometric midpoint of the day's range, most trading happened at low prices (selling pressure absorbed at the lows), which tends to reverse; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Geometric mean of high and low minus VWAP; positive (long) when VWAP is below the range midpoint. Used as in the syntax-fixed file.

description.hypothesis: VWAP below the midpoint of the day's range means most volume traded near the lows (absorbed selling pressure) and tends to reverse; the size of that pressure is the gap relative to price, not in dollars.
description.implementation: Geometric midpoint of high and low minus VWAP, divided by VWAP; long when VWAP sits below the midpoint.

description.hypothesis: VWAP below the day's range midpoint means volume concentrated at the lows (absorbed selling) and reverses; liquidity shocks arrive on high-volume days, so updating only then keeps the reversal while cutting turnover.
description.implementation: Arithmetic range midpoint minus VWAP, as a fraction of VWAP; positions update only when volume exceeds its 20-day average and are held otherwise.

description.hypothesis: A stock whose close has moved toward the top of its daily range over the past nine days has seen building buying pressure that tends to reverse; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Negative 9-day change in ((close - low) - (high - close)) / (close - low), a close-location measure; used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: A stock whose close has moved toward the top of its daily range over nine days has seen building buying pressure that tends to reverse; the close location should be measured on a bounded scale so a single close at the low does not dominate.
description.implementation: Negative 9-day change in the standard close-location value (close position in the day's high-low range, between -1 and 1), with a price-scaled guard against a zero range.

description.hypothesis: Prices revert toward their one-week average, and stocks whose VWAP has tracked the lagged close most closely over about a year (persistent, trending price behaviour) earn a premium; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Scaled gap between the 7-day average close and today's close, plus 20 times the scaled 230-day correlation between VWAP and the 5-day-lagged close; used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: Prices revert toward their one-week average, and the size of the deviation that matters is relative to price, not in dollars; stocks with persistent price tracking over about a year earn a premium.
description.implementation: Same as the baseline but the 7-day mean-reversion gap is divided by the close before scaling; ts_sum(close, 7) / 7 is written as the equivalent ts_mean(close, 7). The 230-day correlation term is unchanged.

description.hypothesis: Stocks whose prices move persistently (VWAP closely tracks the close of five days earlier over about a year) behave differently from choppy, range-bound stocks; this slow characteristic may be the main source of the parent's returns.
description.implementation: The 230-day correlation between VWAP and the 5-day-lagged close on its own, without the 7-day mean-reversion term or scale().

description.hypothesis: Price persistence over about a year is partly a sector trait (some subindustries trend smoothly, others are choppy); the stock-specific part, persistence relative to close peers, is what carries the return premium.
description.implementation: Subtract the subindustry average from each stock's 230-day correlation between VWAP and the 5-day-lagged close.

description.hypothesis: Price-level correlations bunch near +1 with a long negative tail from a few erratic, range-bound stocks, so raw values put outsized short weight on a handful of names; ranking within each subindustry keeps the peer-relative ordering of persistence while spreading risk evenly.
description.implementation: Rank each stock's 230-day correlation between VWAP and the 5-day-lagged close within its subindustry (0 to 1); the simulation's neutralization centres the ranks.

expression: scale(trade_when(volume > ts_mean(volume, 20), (vwap - close) / vwap, -1)) + scale(group_neutralize(ts_corr(vwap, ts_delay(close, 5), 230), subindustry))

description.hypothesis: Daily late-day pressure reversal (alpha042) and slow, year-long price persistence relative to peers (alpha032) are unrelated mechanisms on very different horizons, so their returns should be nearly uncorrelated and an equal-capital blend should have a higher Sharpe than either.
description.implementation: Scale each family's best expression to unit gross exposure and add them, giving equal capital to the volume-gated raw VWAP gap and the subindustry-relative 230-day VWAP/lagged-close correlation.

expression: scale(group_neutralize(ts_corr(vwap, ts_delay(close, 5), 230), subindustry)) + scale((0.5 - rank(group_neutralize(close / ts_delay(close, 7), subindustry))) * (1 + rank(ts_sum(returns, 250))))

description.hypothesis: Slow, year-long price persistence relative to peers and weekly peer-relative reversal with a momentum tilt work on different horizons and information, so an equal-capital blend should raise Sharpe above either leg while avoiding the daily reversal signals that drive the two successful alphas.
description.implementation: Scale each leg to unit gross exposure and add: the subindustry-relative 230-day VWAP/lagged-close correlation, and the centred rank of subindustry-relative 7-day returns times the 1-year momentum multiplier.

expression: scale(group_neutralize(ts_corr(vwap, ts_delay(close, 5), 230), subindustry)) + scale(trade_when(volume > ts_mean(volume, 20), (0.5 - rank(group_neutralize(close / ts_delay(close, 7), subindustry))) * (1 + rank(ts_sum(returns, 250))), -1))

description.hypothesis: Weekly reversal positions only need refreshing when new liquidity shocks arrive on high-volume days; holding them otherwise cuts the weekly leg's turnover without losing its diversifying return, so the blend keeps its Sharpe at much lower turnover.
description.implementation: Same equal-capital blend, but the weekly peer-relative reversal leg updates only when volume exceeds its 20-day average and is held otherwise; the persistence leg is unchanged.

expression: 2 * scale(group_neutralize(ts_corr(vwap, ts_delay(close, 5), 230), subindustry)) + scale((0.5 - rank(group_neutralize(close / ts_delay(close, 7), subindustry))) * (1 + rank(ts_sum(returns, 250))))

description.hypothesis: Equal capital is not the best mix: the persistence leg has the higher Sharpe and almost no turnover, so tilting capital toward it keeps most of the diversification gain while cutting the blend's turnover, which is what fitness needs.
description.implementation: Same two legs as combo_032subind_019subind, with the subindustry-relative persistence leg at twice the capital of the weekly peer-relative reversal leg.

description.hypothesis: If peer-relative price persistence is a genuine stock characteristic, it should be visible over a half-year window as well as the original 230-day window, with similar Sharpe.
description.implementation: Same as a032_corr_subind but the correlation between VWAP and the 5-day-lagged close is measured over 120 days instead of 230.

description.hypothesis: Peer-relative price persistence is a slow stock characteristic, so a longer estimation window should measure it with less noise and give similar or better Sharpe than 230 days.
description.implementation: Same as a032_corr_subind but the correlation between VWAP and the 5-day-lagged close is measured over 500 days.

description.hypothesis: Stocks whose prior-day intraday declines have historically lined up with higher price levels, and stocks that fell intraday today, tend to outperform; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Rank of the 200-day correlation between yesterday's open-minus-close and the close, plus the rank of today's open-minus-close; used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: How a stock's intraday moves relate to its price level over most of a year is a slow characteristic; if slow per-stock correlation traits carry premia (as the alpha032 persistence measure does), this one may too.
description.implementation: The 200-day correlation between yesterday's open-minus-close and the close, without the daily intraday term or rank(). Correlation is scale-free per stock, so dollar units do not matter.

description.hypothesis: Investors anchor on the 52-week high and under-react to good news when the price is near it, so stocks trading close to their 52-week high subsequently outperform those far below it (George and Hwang 2004).
description.implementation: Ratio of today's close to the highest high of the past 250 trading days; long stocks nearest their 52-week high, short those furthest below.

description.hypothesis: Investors anchor on the 52-week high and under-react to good news near it, so stocks trading near the top of their past-year price range outperform those near the bottom (George and Hwang 2004).
description.implementation: Time-series rank of today's close within the past 250 closes (near 1 at a 52-week high, near 0 at a 52-week low).

description.hypothesis: Unusually high trading volume raises a stock's visibility, attracting new investors and demand, so stocks with abnormally high recent volume subsequently outperform (high-volume return premium, Gervais, Kaniel and Mingelgrin 2001).
description.implementation: Rank of average volume over the past week relative to its 60-day average; long the stocks with the most abnormal recent volume.

description.hypothesis: Market- or sector-wide volume surges (macro news, sector rotation) do not raise any single stock's visibility; stock-specific abnormal volume relative to close peers is what attracts new investors and drives the premium.
description.implementation: Subtract the subindustry average from each stock's 5-day/60-day volume ratio before ranking.

description.hypothesis: A price move on rising volume reflects a liquidity shock that reverses next day, while a move on falling volume reflects information that continues; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Opposite of yesterday-to-today price change when volume rose, same direction when volume fell (sign of 1-day volume change times negative 1-day price change); used exactly as provided.

description.hypothesis: More profitable firms earn higher subsequent returns than less profitable firms with similar characteristics, because markets underprice the persistence of profitability (Novy-Marx 2013; Fama and French 2015).
description.implementation: Rank of operating income scaled by total assets; long the most profitable firms relative to their asset base, short the least.

description.hypothesis: Cheap stocks, with high operating earnings relative to market value, outperform expensive ones because investors over-extrapolate past growth and overprice glamour stocks (Lakonishok, Shleifer and Vishny 1994).
description.implementation: Rank of operating income divided by market capitalization (an operating earnings yield); long the cheapest stocks, short the most expensive.

description.hypothesis: The persistence premium comes from how closely a stock's price tracks its own recent path relative to peers; if so, the close alone should capture it and VWAP is incidental.
description.implementation: Same as 1YZOgjpQ but correlating the close (not VWAP) with the 5-day-lagged close over 500 days, relative to the subindustry.

description.hypothesis: If peer-relative price persistence is a general trait of a stock's price path, measuring it against the price a month earlier should show a similar premium to the 5-day lag.
description.implementation: Same as zqbgYJgO but correlating the close with the 20-day-lagged close over 500 days, relative to the subindustry.

description.hypothesis: Peer-relative price persistence (shape of the price path) and the high-volume return premium (investor attention) use unrelated information, so an equal-capital blend should raise Sharpe above the persistence alpha alone at low turnover.
description.implementation: Scale each leg to unit gross exposure and add: subindustry-relative 500-day correlation of the close with its 5-day lag, and the rank of 5-day over 60-day average volume.

description.hypothesis: Firms that grow their total assets fastest subsequently underperform, because investors over-extrapolate past growth and aggressive expansion tends to destroy value (asset-growth effect, Cooper, Gulen and Schill 2008).
description.implementation: Negative rank of total assets relative to their level about one year (250 trading days) earlier; long slow growers, short fast growers.

description.hypothesis: Stocks that fell today, are heavily traded in dollar terms, and closed well below the day's high (a large upper wick, i.e. selling into strength) tend to rebound; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Rank of negative daily return times 20-day average volume times VWAP times (high minus close); used as in the user's file.

expression: trade_when(volume > ts_mean(volume, 20), rank(((((-1 * returns) * ts_mean(volume,20)) * vwap) * (high - close))), -1)

description.hypothesis: The rebound after selling into strength comes from liquidity shocks that arrive on high-volume days; on quiet days the signal changes are mostly noise, so updating only on high-volume days should keep the reversal while cutting turnover.
description.implementation: Wrap the baseline in trade_when: update positions only when volume exceeds its 20-day average, otherwise hold.

expression: trade_when(volume > ts_mean(volume, 20), -returns * (high - close) / close * rank(ts_mean(volume, 20) * vwap), -1)

description.hypothesis: Bigger down-days with larger upper wicks reflect larger liquidity shocks and rebound more, so sizing positions by magnitude rather than rank puts capital where the reversal is strongest; liquid stocks are favoured as in the original.
description.implementation: Negative return times the upper wick as a fraction of the close, times the rank of 20-day dollar volume (bounded liquidity tilt); updated only on high-volume days.

expression: scale(trade_when(volume > ts_mean(volume, 20), rank(((((-1 * returns) * ts_mean(volume,20)) * vwap) * (high - close))), -1)) + scale(group_neutralize(ts_corr(close, ts_delay(close, 5), 500), subindustry))

description.hypothesis: Daily rebound after selling into strength (alpha025) and slow peer-relative price persistence are unrelated mechanisms, so an equal-capital blend should lift Sharpe while the low-turnover persistence leg raises returns per unit of turnover.
description.implementation: Scale each leg to unit gross exposure and add the volume-gated alpha025 rank signal and the subindustry-relative 500-day close persistence.

description.hypothesis: Where the close sits in the day's range, amplified by the open-to-close ratio, captures intraday pressure that reverses; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Negative of (low - close) / (low - high) times (open / close) to the fifth power; used as in the syntax-fixed file.

description.hypothesis: Weekly losers rebound, and the rebound is strongest when recent volume is unusually high (the drop was driven by liquidity demand rather than information); the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: 20-day time-series rank of relative volume times 8-day time-series rank of the negative 7-day price change; used as in the user's file.

description.hypothesis: Weekly losers on unusually high volume rebound; the abnormal-volume condition should be measured over the same weekly horizon as the price move, since single-day volume noise flips the signal daily without adding information.
description.implementation: Replace one-day volume relative to its 20-day average with 5-day average volume relative to its 20-day average; the 7-day reversal term is unchanged.

expression: scale(ts_rank((volume / ts_mean(volume,20)), 20) * ts_rank((-1 * ts_delta(close, 7)), 8)) + scale(group_neutralize(ts_corr(close, ts_delay(close, 5), 500), subindustry))

description.hypothesis: Volume-confirmed weekly reversal (alpha043) and slow peer-relative price persistence are unrelated mechanisms, so an equal-capital blend should raise Sharpe while the near-zero-turnover persistence leg lowers turnover enough for fitness.
description.implementation: Scale each leg to unit gross exposure and add the unchanged Alpha#043 expression and the subindustry-relative 500-day close persistence.

expression: trade_when(volume > ts_mean(volume, 20), ts_rank((volume / ts_mean(volume,20)), 20) * ts_rank((-1 * ts_delta(close, 7)), 8), -1)

description.hypothesis: The volume-confirmed weekly reversal signal is informative mainly on high-volume days, when it is large; on quiet days its changes are noise, so updating only on high-volume days should cut turnover while keeping the reversal.
description.implementation: Wrap the unchanged Alpha#043 expression in trade_when: update positions only when volume exceeds its 20-day average, otherwise hold.

description.hypothesis: Weekly price moves on low recent volume reverse, and the bet is sized up for stocks with strong one-year returns; the source file gives no explanation, so this rationale is the research agent's interpretation.
description.implementation: Negative rank of the 7-day price change weighted by one minus the rank of smoothed relative volume (so low-volume moves count more), times 1 plus the rank of 250-day summed returns; used as in the user's file.
